security_audit.summary: The skill is documentation-only and contains Playwright examples rather than executable automation. Static detections were false positives from Markdown code spans, TypeScript template literals, relative imports, local test URLs, and standard Playwright environment variables. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or malicious system access.

content.value_statement: Playwright tests often become flaky, slow, and noisy in agent workflows. This skill provides concise patterns for locators, assertions, fixtures, auth reuse, network mocks, and compact reporters.
actual_capabilities: Prioritizes resilient Playwright locators such as roles, labels, text, alt text, titles, and test IDs.
Recommends web-first assertions that auto-wait and reduce flaky timing checks.
Shows Page Object Model and fixture patterns for reusable test setup.
Explains auth state reuse, API login setup, and per-test data isolation.
Covers network mocking, Playwright configuration, compact reporters, and common debugging commands.
limitations: It does not run Playwright tests or inspect application behavior by itself.
Examples require adaptation to each application, route structure, and authentication model.
It does not replace a security review of test credentials or stored auth state.
It focuses on Playwright with TypeScript and may not cover every framework integration.

use_cases.title: Stabilize End-to-End Tests
use_cases.description: Improve flaky Playwright tests by replacing brittle selectors, hard waits, and manual assertions with stable test patterns.

use_cases.title: Design Reusable Test Architecture
use_cases.description: Structure page objects, fixtures, helpers, and authentication setup so large suites stay maintainable.

use_cases.title: Tune Agent Test Runs
use_cases.description: Use compact reporters and scoped debugging commands so Claude, Codex, and Claude Code can work with clearer test output.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Playwright Test
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one test file
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Playwright test for flaky selectors, hard waits, and missing web-first assertions. Suggest direct improvements without changing test intent.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Locators
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor these Playwright selectors to prefer roles, labels, text, alt text, titles, or test IDs. Explain any selector that must stay CSS-based.

prompt_templates.title: Build Test Fixtures
prompt_templates.prompt: Design Playwright fixtures and page objects for this user flow. Include setup, teardown, and isolated test data responsibilities.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize a CI Suite
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced suite and agent workflow tuning
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this Playwright configuration for CI and AI agent use. Improve reporters, retries, workers, auth state reuse, traces, and network mocks.

output_examples.input: A test uses CSS selectors, fixed delays, and a shared user record.
output_examples.output: The response identifies brittle selectors, removes fixed waits, and recommends per-test data setup with web-first assertions.

output_examples.input: A team logs in through the UI before every Playwright test.
output_examples.output: The response proposes a setup project that saves authenticated state and reuses it across browser projects.

output_examples.input: An agent receives too much Playwright output during repeated test runs.
output_examples.output: The response recommends compact reporters, focused test commands, and trace capture only when failures need deeper inspection.

best_practices: Prefer user-facing locators before CSS or XPath selectors.
Use web-first assertions so Playwright handles waiting and retry behavior.
Keep each test isolated with its own data and explicit cleanup.
anti_patterns: Avoid fixed timeouts when a locator or assertion can wait for the expected state.
Avoid shared mutable state between tests because order dependence hides failures.
Avoid verbose default reporters in CI or agent sessions when compact output is enough.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps create and review Playwright tests that are stable, readable, and practical for CI or agent workflows.

faq.question: Does it execute Playwright tests?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. A user or agent must run the tests in the target project.

faq.question: Which Playwright patterns does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers locators, web-first assertions, page objects, fixtures, auth state reuse, network mocking, configuration, and debugging.

faq.question: Can it help with flaky tests?
faq.answer: Yes. It focuses on common causes of flakiness, including brittle selectors, hard waits, shared state, and repeated UI login.

faq.question: Is it limited to TypeScript?
faq.answer: The examples use TypeScript with Playwright Test, but many principles apply to other Playwright languages.

faq.question: How should stored auth state be handled?
faq.answer: Store it only for test use, keep it out of source control, and rotate test credentials when needed.
